paper_title: Comparative Study of the Mechanical Properties of All-Polymer and Fullerene-Polymer Solar Cells: The Importance of Polymer Acceptors for High Fracture Resistance

qa_pairs.question: How do the cohesive fracture energy (Gc) values of PTB7-Th:P(NDI2HD-T) all-polymer solar cells compare to PCBM-based solar cells under optimized conditions?
qa_pairs.answer: Under optimized device conditions, all-polymer solar cells (all-PSCs) using PTB7-Th:P(NDI2HD-T) exhibit a cohesive fracture energy (Gc) of 2.45 J/m². This is significantly higher than the 0.29 J/m² observed for PCBM-based solar cells, indicating that the all-polymer system is much more resistant to fracture.
qa_pairs.source_title: Comparative Study of the Mechanical Properties of All-Polymer and Fullerene-Polymer Solar Cells: The Importance of Polymer Acceptors for High Fracture Resistance

qa_pairs.question: What is the difference in crack-onset strain between all-polymer solar cell active layers and PCBM-polymer blend active layers?
qa_pairs.answer: The crack-onset strain for all-polymer solar cell active layers is 15.5 ± 1.2%, which is approximately 15 times higher than the 1.1 ± 0.2% measured for PCBM-polymer blend active layers under optimized efficiency conditions. This demonstrates the superior ductility and mechanical reliability of the all-polymer architecture.
qa_pairs.source_title: Comparative Study of the Mechanical Properties of All-Polymer and Fullerene-Polymer Solar Cells: The Importance of Polymer Acceptors for High Fracture Resistance

qa_pairs.question: How does the concentration of the acceptor material influence the cohesive fracture energy (Gc) in all-polymer solar cells compared to PCBM-based solar cells?
qa_pairs.answer: In all-polymer solar cells, the cohesive fracture energy remains relatively constant at approximately 2.6 J/m² regardless of the polymer acceptor content. In contrast, PCBM-based solar cells show a sharp decrease in fracture energy as the fullerene content increases, indicating that the mechanical integrity of fullerene-based blends is highly sensitive to composition.
qa_pairs.source_title: Comparative Study of the Mechanical Properties of All-Polymer and Fullerene-Polymer Solar Cells: The Importance of Polymer Acceptors for High Fracture Resistance

qa_pairs.question: What underlying mechanisms are responsible for the superior fracture resistance observed in all-polymer solar cell blends?
qa_pairs.answer: The superior fracture resistance is attributed to the inherent ductility of the polymer acceptor and a high degree of plastic deformation during crack growth. This is facilitated by chain entanglement in the mixed domains and the formation of a 'plastic wake' at the crack tip, where polymer chains bridge the crack and require energy-intensive disentanglement (chain pullout) to fail.
qa_pairs.source_title: Comparative Study of the Mechanical Properties of All-Polymer and Fullerene-Polymer Solar Cells: The Importance of Polymer Acceptors for High Fracture Resistance

qa_pairs.question: Which experimental technique is utilized to measure the critical strain energy release rate (Gc) in these polymer solar cell devices?
qa_pairs.answer: The critical strain energy release rate (Gc) of multilayer thin-film polymer solar cell devices is measured using double-cantilever beam (DCB) testing. This method involves applying multiple loading, crack-growth, and unloading cycles to determine the critical energy at the point of the critical load.
qa_pairs.source_title: Comparative Study of the Mechanical Properties of All-Polymer and Fullerene-Polymer Solar Cells: The Importance of Polymer Acceptors for High Fracture Resistance

qa_pairs.question: Compare the stiffness of PTB7-Th:P(NDI2HD-T) all-polymer active layers with PCBM-based active layers using their elastic modulus values.
qa_pairs.answer: All-polymer solar cell active layers under optimized conditions have an elastic modulus of 0.68 ± 0.04 GPa. PCBM-based active layers have a significantly higher modulus of 2.64 ± 0.12 GPa, meaning the PCBM-based layers are nearly four times stiffer and less mechanically compliant than the all-polymer layers.
qa_pairs.source_title: Comparative Study of the Mechanical Properties of All-Polymer and Fullerene-Polymer Solar Cells: The Importance of Polymer Acceptors for High Fracture Resistance

qa_pairs.question: How does Atomic Force Microscopy (AFM) analysis of debonded surfaces help distinguish the fracture behavior of all-PSCs and PCBM-PSCs?
qa_pairs.answer: AFM analysis shows that all-PSCs have high root-mean-square roughness (Rq ~33–35 nm) on debonded surfaces, which indicates significant plastic deformation during failure. Conversely, PCBM-PSCs exhibit very smooth surfaces (Rq ~3–4 nm), which is a characteristic signature of brittle fracture.
qa_pairs.source_title: Comparative Study of the Mechanical Properties of All-Polymer and Fullerene-Polymer Solar Cells: The Importance of Polymer Acceptors for High Fracture Resistance

qa_pairs.question: Why does the fracture path in PCBM-polymer blends shift toward the Aluminum electrode when the acceptor content exceeds 50 wt%?
qa_pairs.answer: The fracture path shifts closer to the Al electrode due to vertical phase separation that forms a polymer-rich skin layer at the surface. This creates a weak interface between the polymer-rich phase and the aggregated PCBM-rich domains, providing a low-energy pathway for crack propagation.
qa_pairs.source_title: Comparative Study of the Mechanical Properties of All-Polymer and Fullerene-Polymer Solar Cells: The Importance of Polymer Acceptors for High Fracture Resistance
